mocodes.label: Music – Faculty Travel
mocodes.why: Faculty conference travel, professional meetings, accreditation activity, research travel, and related professional development expenses.

mocodes.label: Music – Faculty Searches
mocodes.why: Faculty recruitment, candidate travel, onboarding support, search processes, and faculty hiring-related operational expenses.

mocodes.label: Music – Instructional Support
mocodes.why: Instructional supplies, classroom and studio materials, curriculum support resources, and academic instructional expenses.

ambiguity.guidance: Use M-03 for materials used in teaching (method books, classroom supplies). Use M-15 for music purchased specifically for ensemble performance or concerts.

mocodes.label: Music – Student Recruitment
mocodes.why: Recruitment travel, auditions, campus visit events, admissions operations, recruiting materials, and student outreach efforts.

mocodes.label: Music – External Relations
mocodes.why: Marketing, communications, donor relations, fundraising support, public-facing events, and external relations operations for the Music division.

mocodes.label: Music – Visiting Artists (Academic)
mocodes.why: Guest artists, masterclasses, lecturers, clinicians, and residencies supporting curricular activity. For production guest artists, use Music Productions (MP-01).

ambiguity.guidance: Use M-06 when the guest artist is visiting for a masterclass, residency, or curricular purpose. Use MP-01 when the artist is performing in or directing a specific production.

mocodes.label: Music – Office Operations
mocodes.why: Office supplies, postage, printing, duplication, and day-to-day administrative operations of the Music division.

mocodes.label: Music – Technical Services
mocodes.why: Instrument maintenance, piano tuning, equipment repair, and related technical support services. Distinct from Technology Services (M-11).

mocodes.label: Music – Student Operational Workers
mocodes.why: Admin, front desk, technical, and non-academic student worker roles. Not accompanists (TBDP1), or curricular student workers (TBDP25).

ambiguity.also: M-13 Accompanist Services or M-14 Curricular Student Worker Support
ambiguity.guidance: Use M-09 for students in operational/administrative roles (front desk, office help, non-academic tech). Use M-13 for student accompanists. Use M-14 for students in ensemble conducting or other curricular support roles.

mocodes.notes: Compensation flow — triggered by worker type selection

mocodes.label: Music – Equipment
mocodes.why: Equipment purchases, rentals, leases, repairs, replacements, and operational equipment support activity.

ambiguity.guidance: Use M-10 for purchasing or replacing equipment. Use M-08 for repairing or maintaining instruments and equipment (piano tuning, instrument repair).

mocodes.label: Music – Technology
mocodes.why: Software licenses, electronic media systems, instructional technology, digital platforms, computing support, and technology-related operational services.

mocodes.label: Music – Student Touring
mocodes.why: Ensemble tours, conference attendance, student competition travel, off-campus performances, and related student travel activity.

mocodes.label: Music – Accompanist Services

examples: Student academic worker in accompanying role

mocodes.why: Student academic workers serving as accompanists supporting instructional activity, rehearsals, classes, coaching, and performance preparation.
mocodes.notes: Compensation flow — triggered by worker type selection. Account 703800 identifies these as student academic workers.

mocodes.label: Music – Curricular Student Worker Support
mocodes.why: Student worker positions providing curricular support, including ensemble conducting. Replaces old program K8971 (CONDUCTING ENSEMBLE). Do not use TBDP24/707100 for these positions.
mocodes.notes: Compensation flow — triggered by worker type selection.

mocodes.label: Music – Performance Materials
mocodes.why: Performance scores, ensemble music purchases, sheet music rentals, and related music library and performance materials. Program identifier (TBDP26) is pending final assignment from K8967–K8984 range.

ambiguity.guidance: Use M-15 for music purchased for ensemble performance or concerts. Use M-03 for music or materials used primarily in classroom instruction (method books, theory texts).

mocodes.notes: TBDP26 identifier is TBD — update program code in this file when final assignment is confirmed.

mocodes.label: Music Productions – General Production

examples: Equipment maintenance tied to a specific show

mocodes.why: All production expenses for music productions including costumes, scenic, lighting/sound, overhire labor, royalties, and guest artists. NASM HEADS VI.A reports one total — Account identifies the expense type. Individual shows add a Project code on top of this MoCode.

ambiguity.guidance: Use MP-01 when the guest artist is performing in or directing a specific production. Use M-06 when the artist is visiting for a masterclass, residency, or curricular purpose unrelated to a specific show.

mocodes.notes: Individual shows add a Project code. Royalties and licensing are folded into this MoCode via Account 750000 or 750900.

mocodes.label: Theatre – Faculty Travel
mocodes.why: Faculty conference travel, professional meetings, accreditation activity, research travel, and related professional development expenses.

mocodes.why: Office supplies, postage, printing, duplication, and day-to-day administrative operations of the Theatre division.

mocodes.why: Maintenance and repair of technical infrastructure including lighting boards, sound systems, rigging, and related equipment. Distinct from Technology Services (TO-11).

mocodes.label: Theatre – Student Operational Workers
mocodes.why: Admin, front desk, technical, and non-academic student worker roles. Account 707100 identifies as non-academic student employees.

mocodes.why: Equipment purchases, rentals, leases, repairs, replacements, and operational equipment support activity.

mocodes.label: Theatre Productions – Performance Operations
mocodes.why: Production coordination, guest directors, designers, and contracted artists for specific productions. NAST HEADS VI.A.2 reports one production total. Individual shows use a Project code on top of this MoCode.

ambiguity.guidance: Use TP-01 when the artist is a director, designer, or performer engaged for a specific production. Use TO-06 when the guest artist is visiting for a masterclass or curricular residency.

mocodes.notes: Individual shows add a Project code. NAST requires a production count — each Project code represents one production.

mocodes.label: Theatre Productions – Costumes & Wardrobe
mocodes.why: Costume purchases, rentals, alterations, wardrobe supplies, hair and makeup support, and related production costume activity.
mocodes.notes: Individual shows add a Project code.

mocodes.label: Theatre Productions – Scenic & Production Materials
mocodes.why: Scenery, props, staging materials, lumber, paint, fabrication supplies, rehearsal materials, and related production support materials.
mocodes.notes: Individual shows add a Project code.

mocodes.label: Theatre Productions – Lighting, Sound & Stage Support
mocodes.why: Lighting systems, audio support, stage operations, projections, and backstage support for specific productions.
mocodes.notes: Individual shows add a Project code.

mocodes.label: Theatre Productions – General Production Labor
mocodes.why: Overhire labor, stagehands, run crews, and temporary technical staffing shared across productions — not specific to one show. For labor tied to a specific show, use a Project code on TP-01.

ambiguity.guidance: Use TP-05 (Project = 00) for labor that serves multiple shows or the season generally — e.g., a stagehand hired for the whole season. Use TP-01 with a Project code for labor engaged specifically for one production.

mocodes.notes: NOT for use on specific theatre shows. Use Project = 00.

mocodes.label: Theatre Productions – Royalties & Licensing
mocodes.why: Performance rights, script licensing, choreography licensing, music licensing, and other production-related royalty and intellectual property expenses.
mocodes.notes: Individual shows add a Project code.

compensationRules.programNote: Music: always use Program TBDP1 — MoCode M-13. Dance: always use Program TBDP1 — MoCode D-12.
compensationRules.why: Student academic workers serving as accompanists are coded to TBDP1 in both Music and Dance. Account 703800 identifies the student academic worker category.
examples: Student pianist for a Dance technique class
Student piano accompanist for studio class

compensationRules.workerType: Curricular student worker — Music (ensemble conducting, curricular support)
compensationRules.programNote: Always use Program TBDP25 — MoCode M-14. Do NOT use TBDP24 (707100) for these positions.
compensationRules.why: Student workers in curricular support roles (including ensemble conducting) use TBDP25. This replaces old program K8971 (CONDUCTING ENSEMBLE). Account 703800 identifies the student academic worker category.
examples: Student assigned to conduct an ensemble
Student in a curricular support role

compensationRules.workerType: Student operational worker (admin, front desk, tech support)
compensationRules.programNote: Always use Program TBDP24. Use the divisional DeptID (K1306001, K1305002, K0923001) matching where the student works.
compensationRules.why: Non-academic student workers in admin, front desk, technical, and operational roles use Account 707100 and Program TBDP24. Distinct from academic student workers (703800).
examples: Student helping with non-academic technical tasks

compensationRules.programNote: Use the relevant production MoCode for that division — TP-01, TP-05, DP-01, MP-01, or PA-02. Add a Project code for show-specific labor.
compensationRules.why: Production overhire and stagehands are coded as part-time staff (705500) or overtime (708050) under the production Program and DeptID for that division.
examples: Production labor for a specific show
